paragraphs.source_en: To return to the main subject, let me report to you the curious tale of how this open space became the source of the disturbance. But on no account tell my master; this is as far as the story goes. To begin with, the greatest inconvenience of this vacant lot was that it had no fence. It was an open space through which the wind blew every which way, liable to sweep things off at any moment, and across which anyone could freely pass without needing anyone's permission. Even the word “free” hardly seems quite accurate. To tell the truth, unless one begins from the very beginning, the cause of the matter cannot be understood. And if the cause is not known, even a doctor will be at a loss for a prescription. I must therefore begin leisurely from the time when my master first moved here. With the wind passing through it this way and that, the open lot was cool in summer and exceedingly pleasant. As for its being insecure, in the house of a poor teacher there could hardly be any fear of burglary. Thus at my master's house, walls, fences, palisades, chevaux-de-frise, and all such things were wholly unnecessary. But I think that depends on what sort of people, or animals, live on the far side of the open ground. Consequently, to answer this question, one must necessarily clarify the nature of the gentlemen stationed opposite. It may be rather hasty to call them gentlemen before it is clear whether they are human beings or animals, but in the main one will not go wrong in calling them gentlemen. For in this world there are people called gentlemen of the beams, and even thieves can be called gentlemen. Of course, the gentlemen I speak of here differ from gentlemen of the beams and will not trouble the police. Yet as far as numbers go, there seems to be plenty to discuss: they are truly as plentiful as fish in a river crossing. This was a private middle school called Rakuunkan, with eight hundred gentlemen in all. The school collected a monthly tuition fee of two yen in order to cultivate these remarkable gentlemen into still greater gentlemen. Because its name is Rakuunkan, perhaps some people may imagine its students are all elegant, refined gentlemen. In fact, that is not so; it is just as unreliable as assuming cranes descend at Gunkakukan, or as finding a cat in Garyukutsu. Since you understand that among those styled scholars or teachers there are mad fellows like my master Kushami, you should naturally also understand that the gentlemen of Rakuunkan are not all men of refined taste. If any of you say, “I do not believe it,” then first come and stay at my master's house for three days or so.

units.source_en: To return to the main subject, let me report to you the curious tale of how this open space became the source of the disturbance.
units.source_zh: 言归正传，且让我向诸位禀报一下这块地方是如何成为闹事根源的有趣故事。

units.source_en: But on no account tell my master; this is as far as the story goes.

ja.t: にいってはいけない。これぎりの

units.source_zh: 不过，这可千万不要对主人说，我说到哪里就是哪里。

units.source_en: To begin with, the greatest inconvenience of this vacant lot was that it had no fence.
units.source_zh: 先说这块空地吧，最大的不方便之处，是它没有墙。

units.source_en: It was an open space through which the wind blew every which way, liable to sweep things off at any moment, and across which anyone could freely pass without needing anyone's permission.
units.source_zh: 这是一块风刮来刮去随时都可以刮跑东西的空地，是任何人不需要获得任何许可就可以自由横穿的一块空地。

units.source_en: Even the word “free” hardly seems quite accurate.
units.source_zh: 用“自由”两字似乎还不确切。

units.source_zh: 老实说，事情如果不从原本说起，是无法了解它的起因的。

units.source_en: And if the cause is not known, even a doctor will be at a loss for a prescription.
units.source_zh: 如果起因不明，连大夫也无法对症下药。

units.source_en: I must therefore begin leisurely from the time when my master first moved here.
units.source_zh: 所以我必须从主人搬到这里的当时慢慢向各位道来。

units.source_en: With the wind passing through it this way and that, the open lot was cool in summer and exceedingly pleasant.
units.source_zh: 这块空地风吹过来吹过去，夏天是很凉快的，使人十分舒坦。

units.source_en: As for its being insecure, in the house of a poor teacher there could hardly be any fear of burglary.
units.source_zh: 至于不严紧嘛，一个穷教员家，也不会有被盗之虞。

units.source_en: Thus at my master's house, walls, fences, palisades, chevaux-de-frise, and all such things were wholly unnecessary.
units.source_zh: 因此主人的房子，一切墙、篱笆以及什么梅花桩、鹿角桩之类，都是不需要的。

units.source_en: But I think that depends on what sort of people, or animals, live on the far side of the open ground.
units.source_zh: 但是我却认为这要取决于住在空地对面的人或动物是属于哪一种类。

units.source_en: Consequently, to answer this question, one must necessarily clarify the nature of the gentlemen stationed opposite.

ja.t: かにせんければならん。

units.source_zh: 因此，为了回答这个问题，必然要弄明白对面那些君子们的性质。

units.source_en: It may be rather hasty to call them gentlemen before it is clear whether they are human beings or animals, but in the main one will not go wrong in calling them gentlemen.
units.source_zh: 还未弄清是人还是动物之前，就把他们称为君子，未免太性急了，不过，称他们为君子大体上是不会有错的。

units.source_en: For in this world there are people called gentlemen of the beams, and even thieves can be called gentlemen.
units.source_zh: 因为现在社会上有一种称为梁上君子的人，连这种偷鸡摸狗的人都可以称为君子嘛。

units.source_en: Of course, the gentlemen I speak of here differ from gentlemen of the beams and will not trouble the police.
units.source_zh: 当然，这里所说的君子不同于梁上君子，是不会麻烦警察的。

units.source_en: Yet as far as numbers go, there seems to be plenty to discuss: they are truly as plentiful as fish in a river crossing.

ja.t: いる。うじゃうじゃいる。

units.source_zh: 不过，看来他们在数量上却大有文章可做，真算得上是多如过江之鲫。

units.source_en: This was a private middle school called Rakuunkan, with eight hundred gentlemen in all.
units.source_zh: 这是一所叫做“落云馆”的私立中学，一共有八百位君子。

units.source_en: The school collected a monthly tuition fee of two yen in order to cultivate these remarkable gentlemen into still greater gentlemen.
units.source_zh: 这所学校为了培养这些了不起的君子，每月收两元钱的学费。

units.source_en: Because its name is Rakuunkan, perhaps some people may imagine its students are all elegant, refined gentlemen.
units.source_zh: 由于名称是落云馆，也许有人会认为这里的学生都是一些风流潇洒的君子。

units.source_en: In fact, that is not so; it is just as unreliable as assuming cranes descend at Gunkakukan, or as finding a cat in Garyukutsu.

ja.t: がいるようなものである。

units.source_zh: 其实不然，其不可信之处，正如群鹤馆不会真的有白鹤飞来，卧龙窟中居然有猫儿一样。

units.source_en: Since you understand that among those styled scholars or teachers there are mad fellows like my master Kushami, you should naturally also understand that the gentlemen of Rakuunkan are not all men of refined taste.
units.source_zh: 既然诸位了解号称学士或教师当中有苦沙弥这样疯疯癫癫的人，那么当然也应该了解落云馆里的君子们并不都是风流汉。

units.source_en: If any of you say, “I do not believe it,” then first come and stay at my master's house for three days or so.
units.source_zh: 如果诸位当中有人说“我不信”，那就先请到主人家里来呆上三天好啰。

paragraphs.source_zh: 言归正传，且让我向诸位禀报一下这块地方是如何成为闹事根源的有趣故事。不过，这可千万不要对主人说，我说到哪里就是哪里。先说这块空地吧，最大的不方便之处，是它没有墙。这是一块风刮来刮去随时都可以刮跑东西的空地，是任何人不需要获得任何许可就可以自由横穿的一块空地。用“自由”两字似乎还不确切。老实说，事情如果不从原本说起，是无法了解它的起因的。如果起因不明，连大夫也无法对症下药。所以我必须从主人搬到这里的当时慢慢向各位道来。这块空地风吹过来吹过去，夏天是很凉快的，使人十分舒坦。至于不严紧嘛，一个穷教员家，也不会有被盗之虞。因此主人的房子，一切墙、篱笆以及什么梅花桩、鹿角桩之类，都是不需要的。但是我却认为这要取决于住在空地对面的人或动物是属于哪一种类。因此，为了回答这个问题，必然要弄明白对面那些君子们的性质。还未弄清是人还是动物之前，就把他们称为君子，未免太性急了，不过，称他们为君子大体上是不会有错的。因为现在社会上有一种称为梁上君子的人，连这种偷鸡摸狗的人都可以称为君子嘛。当然，这里所说的君子不同于梁上君子，是不会麻烦警察的。不过，看来他们在数量上却大有文章可做，真算得上是多如过江之鲫。这是一所叫做“落云馆”的私立中学，一共有八百位君子。这所学校为了培养这些了不起的君子，每月收两元钱的学费。由于名称是落云馆，也许有人会认为这里的学生都是一些风流潇洒的君子。其实不然，其不可信之处，正如群鹤馆不会真的有白鹤飞来，卧龙窟中居然有猫儿一样。既然诸位了解号称学士或教师当中有苦沙弥这样疯疯癫癫的人，那么当然也应该了解落云馆里的君子们并不都是风流汉。如果诸位当中有人说“我不信”，那就先请到主人家里来呆上三天好啰。
